newsitem.title: USA: U.S. troops waiting for order to deploy to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops waiting for order to deploy to Gulf.

text.p: The planned deployment of army troops from Texas to join a U.S. military buildup in the Gulf region was on hold on Sunday as Kuwait's leaders discussed whether to allow the soldiers onto their soil.

Defense officials at Fort Hood, about 120 miles (200 km) south of Dallas, said 3,000 soldiers were ready to go but that the original plan to send them off this weekend was delayed and it was possible they might not go at all.
"If we get the order, we expect it'll probably be on Tuesday," said Staff Sergeant Monica McNeal, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Army's Fort Hood base in central Texas.

The Clinton administration on Friday announced it had ordered 5,000 army troops from Fort Hood to join forces already in the Gulf as the United States reacted to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's military incursion into the Kurdish-controlled area in northern Iraq and missile-firings at U.S. warplanes.

U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry, on a visit to the Gulf to rally the Gulf War alliance against Saddam, on Sunday asked Kuwait's emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, for permission to proceed with the plan to deploy the Fort Hood troops.
Perry said the emir replied that a decision would be made after Kuwait's Supreme Defense Council discussed the issue.

The Fort Hood troops -- members of two battalions and a Brigade Combat Team headquarters as well as backup maintenance and medical staff -- would be deployed under Exercise Intrinsic Action, a program begun last year to train Kuwaiti soldiers.
About 1,200 soldiers have been in Kuwait since August under the same program.
The Pentagon said 5,000 troops would be deployed from Fort Hood but officials at the base said only about 3,000 were needed to fully comply with the mission's requirements.
"When we got the requirements, we started filling the bill based on what they said they need, and our count is about 3,000," McNeal said.

While the Fort Hood ground troops would formally be on a training mission in Kuwait, their deployment was clearly aimed at boosting the buildup of U.S. military planes, warships and ground forces for possible attacks against Iraq.
But Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Jaber al-Sabah said there was no question of U.S. land forces crossing into Iraq from Kuwait.

"There is no passage for land forces, but there are air forces at Kuwaiti bases and this is not something new and they are also present in other states in the Gulf," he told reporters in the Egyptian city of Alexandria.

Eight radar-dodging Stealth warplanes, four U.S. B-52 bombers with cruise missiles and an aircraft carriers have been deployed to the Gulf in recent days, as well as two batteries of anti-missile Patriot missiles.
